changes.before: Replace NULL with NA. What length prints?
changes.after: NULL means no object value here. It has length zero. NA stands for one missing entry.

before: NULL is a special null object with length zero. NA is a missing value that can occupy an element position.
numeric(0) creates an empty double vector, whereas character(0) creates empty text storage. Both have length zero but are not identical types.
length reports how many entries an object contains; it is not the amount of text used to print the object.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
value <- NULL
cat(length(value))
```

after.question: What length does a single NA have?
after.explanation: One position exists even when its value is unknown.
